description: The observer in `¬$x.following-tokens.begins(term)` reads the original input through the span projection. The chosen a elides T at 0 and at 2, so the reconstructed input is T A B T, and c reads both synthetic T as bare terminals. a survives only if $x.following-tokens is the empty original suffix; then a and c are two readings. Read over the reconstructed tokens, $x.following-tokens begins with the trailing synthetic T, which term reads, a is lost, and c alone would pass (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a ([+T="ta"] $x:pair [+T="ta"]) %conditions ¬($x.following-tokens.begins(term))

%rule b ([+T="ta"] [+T="ta"] pair [+T="ta"])
%rule c (T="ta" pair T="ta")
%rule pair (A B)
%rule term T
